lesson.title: Why a squared plus b squared is c squared
lesson.goal: See that on a right triangle the squares on the two short sides together hold exactly as many unit squares as the square on the long side, first by counting the 3-4-5 triangle, then by sliding four triangles around.

say: This is a right triangle. It has one square corner, and two short sides next to it. The short sides are three and four long. The long side across from the corner is the hypotenuse.
Build a square on the side of length three. Each side of that square is three long, so it holds three rows of three little unit squares. Count them as they light up: nine.
Now the square on the side of length four. It holds four rows of four. Count them as they light up: sixteen.
Last, the square on the long side. It is five long, so it holds five rows of five. Count them as they light up: twenty-five.
Nine plus sixteen is twenty-five. Watch the unit squares from the two short sides slide into the big square. They fill it exactly, with nothing left over.

Is that luck for three, four and five? Here is a different way to see it. Take four copies of this triangle, and set them inside a big square with sides a plus b. The space left in the middle is a tilted square on the long side.

Now slide the triangles to the other corners, without turning them. The big square is the same size, and the four triangles are the same size, so the space left over must be the same too. But now it is two squares, one on each short side.
So the tilted square on the long side has exactly the same area as the two squares on the short sides together. That works for any right triangle. A squared plus b squared equals c squared.
Try it on a bigger triangle with short sides six and eight. The squares on them hold thirty-six and sixty-four unit squares. Before I build the last square, predict: how long is the long side?

challenge.prompt: How long is the long side of the six and eight triangle?

say: The long side is ten. Its square holds one hundred unit squares. Now slide the two small squares in. They fill it exactly, because thirty-six plus sixty-four is one hundred.

practice.rule: In a right triangle, the areas of the squares on the two short sides add up to the area of the square on the long side
practice.condition: the triangle has a square corner

challenges.say: Tell me why the two small squares always fill the big square exactly, with a because.
Here is a corner that is open wider than a square corner. If two sides meet there, does a squared plus b squared still equal c squared?
Now a right triangle with short sides five and twelve. How long is the long side?

challenge.prompt: How long is the long side of the five and twelve triangle?
